summary: Remote shell, RCE, and arbitrary filesystem access via hardcoded WebSocket C2 (pull.7ii.win:7999)
details: newtun connects on startup to a hardcoded WebSocket server (default pull.7ii.win:7999) and exposes three server-driven primitives to that remote peer. (1) Backdoor shell: on TERM_OPEN messages, TunnelClient spawns a PTY (bash on Unix, cmd.exe on Windows) via node-pty and pipes base64-decoded bytes from the server into term.write(), giving the remote peer an interactive shell under the installer's user account. (2) Arbitrary command execution: on SCRIPT_LIST / POLICY_SCRIPTS messages, executeScript() passes the server-supplied `content` string directly to child_process.exec and returns stdout, stderr, and exit code, letting the server run any command. (3) Arbitrary filesystem access: handleFileRequest implements list/read/write/delete/mkdir/rename/stat over server-supplied paths with no restriction, letting the server exfiltrate files up to 10MB and overwrite arbitrary paths. Together these are a fully-featured remote-access trojan controlled by whoever operates pull.7ii.win.
